author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, on a single page reachable only at its own address.
acceptance_criteria: Opening the specialty directory lists every specialty the clinic knows, by its stored name.
Each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
Every specialty renders together on one page; nothing offers a further page.
No other page of the system carries a link to the specialty directory.
Edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by no one.
Edge case 2: with no specialties at all, the page opens with an empty list rather than failing.
Edge case 3: specialties are listed in a stable order, and so are the veterinarians under each.
non_goals: Managing veterinarians or their specialties through the application — NG-2 is unchanged
A navigation entry or a link from any other page to the specialty directory; a visible entry point may come as a follow-up request
Searching or filtering the specialty list — NG-9 stands
notes: Product-fixed address: GET /specialties.html. REQ-VET-002 is withdrawn (Superseded list) and is never reused; this requirement takes REQ-VET-003. The dispatch-start at line 1 carries the wrong req_id (REQ-VET-002), minted before the Superseded list was read; the dispatch-start at line 2 supersedes it and no work was done under REQ-VET-002. REQ-LANG-002 binds this slice: every new piece of page wording needs a message key present in all eleven bundles, and none may be hard-coded in the template. REQ-SYS-001 is unaffected — the new page still carries the standard navigation to owner search and the veterinarian directory; what is excluded is a navigation entry pointing at this page. Autofix audit: no prd-autofix records in the log. Three open questions recorded in docs/prd.md (visible entry point, list order, unheld specialties); each took the narrowest reading rather than blocking.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: The slice stays inside the vet feature package: it adds a third route to that package's web surface and reads the two entities already mapped there. One thing is new ground. Every page in this codebase today hands entities straight to a template, and this page's shape (specialty to its holders) is the inverse of the JPA mapping, which is owned by Vet alone. That is recorded as a new pattern in docs/system-design.md#read-models, backed by a new ADR: a page whose shape is not an entity or a list of entities gets an immutable read model, built by a static factory from repository results, carrying the ordering and formatting; the controller reads, delegates, and selects the view. Everything else the slice needs is covered by existing memory: the feature-package layout, the direct controller-to-repository dependency, the Thymeleaf layout fragment, and the message-bundle rule for REQ-LANG-002. Three names are binding, since the Contracts table now carries them: SpecialtyController, SpecialtyRepository, SpecialtyDirectory, all in the vet package.
integration_points: SpecialtyController maps GET /specialties.html, reads SpecialtyRepository and the existing VetRepository.findAll(), and puts one SpecialtyDirectory on the model under a single attribute; view name vets/specialtyList.

SpecialtyDirectory is built by a static factory taking the specialty collection and the veterinarian collection; it exposes entries of (specialty name, ordered list of holder full names) and holds no entity reference.
SpecialtyRepository is a new Spring Data repository over the already-mapped specialties table; it adds no schema and no mapping change.

The template calls the shared layout fragment. It must pass a menu argument that matches no existing menu item (for example 'specialties'), so the Veterinarians nav entry is not highlighted, and fragments/layout.html gains no entry (REQ-SYS-001 nav unchanged, and the slice's non-goal on a navigation entry).

patterns.description: Lookup repository returning its rows in name order via an explicit @Query. SpecialtyRepository follows this shape exactly; it is the ordering source for the specialty list.

Package-private @Controller with constructor-injected repositories, a @GetMapping per route, and a returned view name. SpecialtyController follows it; a separate controller per domain noun matches the owner package (OwnerController, PetController, VisitController).
The Vet-to-Specialty association: @ManyToMany(fetch = EAGER) owned by Vet, no inverse side on Specialty. This is the fetch strategy the directory relies on and must not change.
Existing rendering of a holder-less case with the #{none} key. Reuse it for a specialty no veterinarian holds; the key already exists in every bundle.

Two build-time gates for REQ-LANG-002: literal text between tags in any src/main HTML fails the build, and every key in messages.properties must exist in the nine locale bundles (messages_en.properties is intentionally empty and skipped).

risks.risk: Reaching the holders from Specialty by adding @ManyToMany(mappedBy = "specialties") on Specialty. This puts a cycle into the graph the /vets route serializes (Vet to Specialty to Vet), and spring.jpa.open-in-view is disabled, so a lazy inverse side would fail during render.
risks.mitigation: Do not touch the mapping. Read specialties and veterinarians separately and invert in SpecialtyDirectory. Recorded in docs/system-design.md#read-models and the ADR.

risks.risk: N+1 concern prompting a JOIN FETCH on the veterinarian read. The eager Set does issue a collection load per veterinarian, but spring.jpa.properties.hibernate.default_batch_fetch_size=16 batches them and VetRepository.findAll() is @Cacheable("vets").
risks.mitigation: Reuse the existing VetRepository.findAll() unchanged. Add no query and no fetch join in this slice; a fetch join would in any case be admissible only on an unpaged query, never on the paged findAll(Pageable), which Hibernate would then paginate in memory.

risks.risk: Adding @Cacheable to the new specialty read. The vets cache has no eviction configured, which is already open question 5 in docs/system-design.md; a second cached read widens it for no requirement.
risks.mitigation: Leave SpecialtyRepository uncached. The Contracts row states this.

risks.risk: New wording added to the template without a key, or with a key missing from a locale bundle, fails the build under I18nPropertiesSyncTest.
risks.mitigation: The page needs no new key: #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{name}, and #{none} all exist. If new wording is genuinely needed, add the key to messages.properties and to the nine locale bundles (de, es, fa, hi, ja, ko, pt, ru, tr); leave messages_en.properties empty.

risks.risk: Grouping and ordering ending up in the controller or the template, which would put the slice's three edge-case criteria behind MVC infrastructure and add logic to a controller that architecture-principles.md forbids for new rules.
risks.mitigation: The read model owns the inversion, the comparators, and the first-name-then-last-name formatting, so those criteria are provable with real Vet and Specialty objects and no stub.

notes:
Autofix audit: no design-doc-autofix records in the log; nothing to audit.

Ordering (acceptance criterion 8, open in the PRD): specialties by name, taken from SpecialtyRepository's ORDER BY, matching PetTypeRepository and Vet.getSpecialties(). Holders by last name then first name, with a final tiebreak on id so equal names never reorder. The comparators live in SpecialtyDirectory, in one place, and are asserted there. The specific keys are not load-bearing; determinism and single ownership are.

View model shape: SpecialtyDirectory is a record (or a record carrying a List of a nested entry record) with a static factory of(Collection<Specialty>, Collection<Vet>). Entries hold the stored specialty name and a List<String> of already-formatted holder full names ("Helen Leary"). Lists are copied on construction (List.copyOf). No entity leaks into the model attribute, which keeps rendering safe under spring.jpa.open-in-view=false. A specialty no one holds gets an empty holder list, which the template renders with #{none}; no specialties at all gives an empty entry list, which renders an empty table body rather than an error, so no null branch is needed anywhere.

Path redirection from the prd-entry's file_targets: the page gets its own SpecialtyController and SpecialtyControllerTests rather than extending VetController and VetControllerTests, matching the owner package's one-controller-per-domain-noun shape and keeping @WebMvcTest isolation. VetController and VetRepository are unchanged; VetRepository.findAll() is consumed as it stands.

Test seam: most of the seven test names are behavior of SpecialtyDirectory and belong in SpecialtyDirectoryTests with real objects and no stub, per testing-principles.md's mocking policy. The controller test covers route, view name, and model attribute; the seeded H2 data (radiology, surgery, dentistry) also supports an end-to-end check in the PetClinicIntegrationTests style if the test designer wants one. Final test allocation is the test designer's call.

Vocabulary: "specialty directory" is the PRD's phrase and is not yet in docs/ubiquitous-language.md. That file is the product-requirements-expert's; flagging it as a follow-up, not blocking this slice.

Durable memory written: docs/adr/2026-08-23-read-models-for-non-entity-page-shapes.md (new, indexed in docs/adr/README.md), and docs/system-design.md gained a Read models subsection plus three Contracts rows.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Injection: SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() uses a fixed JPQL string constant in @Query with no parameters, no bind variables, and no concatenation. The route takes no request parameter, path variable, header, or form input at all, so no attacker-controlled value reaches the query builder. Swept the change set for dynamic query construction (createQuery/createNativeQuery/String concatenation into JPQL or SQL, @Query with SpEL fragments) - no other instance.

XSS: every user-derived value in templates/vets/specialtyList.html is rendered through th:text, which HTML-escapes by default. Specialty names (${entry.name}), holder full names (${holder + ' '}), and the message-key headers are all escaped. Swept the new template for the unescaped-output class - no th:utext, no th:attr writing into a javascript: or on* handler, no th:inline='javascript' block, no th:href/th:src carrying a model value. Thymeleaf escaping is not disabled anywhere in the change set.

Data escape into the model: the only model attribute is specialtyDirectory, a SpecialtyDirectory record holding List<Entry> of (String name, List<String> holders). No JPA entity, no proxy, and no repository reference reaches the model or the template, so no lazy traversal and no over-exposure of entity fields. Both record constructors defensively copy with List.copyOf, and SpecialtyDirectoryTests asserts the read model does not change when its source collections mutate.

Serialization: SpecialtyController returns a view name with no @ResponseBody and no @RestController, so the read model is never serialized to JSON or XML - the page has no serialized representation to leak through content negotiation.

/vets JSON graph unaffected: Specialty.java and Vet.java are not in the change set. Verified directly - Specialty still extends NamedEntity with no inverse mapping, and the sole @ManyToMany remains the owning side on Vet. No cycle was introduced into the graph the /vets route serializes, matching the ADR's stated rejection of option 1.

Unauthenticated route: /specialties.html adds a read-only GET that inherits the application-wide absence of authentication already recorded in docs/system-design.md Threat Model row 1. It exposes no new data class - specialty names and veterinarian full names are already public on /vets.html and the /vets serialized route. No PII beyond what is already published, no identifiers, no operational detail. Pre-existing posture, not a new exposure.

Secrets: swept the full change set for credential material by name and by shape (token, password, secret, key, credential, passwd, pwd, api, bearer, datasource). No hit in the added Java, template, or test sources. No property file, compose file, or manifest is touched.

Supply chain: no dependency change. build.gradle, pom.xml, and gradle/ are unmodified in the change set, so no new coordinate, no version bump, and no new transitive surface enters the build. No CVE surface is introduced by this slice.

author: code-quality-reviewer
approved_aspects: SpecialtyController stays a thin delegator (constructor injection, one @GetMapping, no logic) matching VetController's shape.
SpecialtyRepository.findSpecialties() mirrors PetTypeRepository.findPetTypes() exactly (name-ordered @Query) and is deliberately left uncached, per the design's caching risk note.

SpecialtyDirectory and its nested Entry are true value objects: immutable records, List.copyOf on every constructed collection, static factory `of(...)`, typed fields (no raw Object/Map<String,Object> escaping), and no entity reference leaves the model.

Ordering is owned entirely by the read model via two well-documented Comparator constants (BY_SPECIALTY_NAME, BY_HOLDER_NAME) with explicit id tiebreaks, keeping the three edge-case behaviors (empty holders, empty directory, stable order) provable with plain objects and no MVC or persistence stub.

Template (specialtyList.html) follows vetList.html's existing holder-rendering idiom exactly, iterates only the prepared Entry list, and passes 'specialties' as the layout menu argument, which matches no existing menuItem (home, owners, vets, error) -- correctly leaving the Veterinarians nav unhighlighted.
No new i18n keys were needed or added; #{specialties}, #{vets}, #{name}, #{none} are all pre-existing keys, avoiding any I18nPropertiesSyncTest risk.
./gradlew checkFormatMain checkFormatTest and compileJava/compileTestJava all pass clean; no formatting issues.

The new ClinicServiceTests repository-ordering test for SpecialtyRepository follows the same convention already used there for PetTypeRepository, so the added coverage sits in an established location rather than a new one.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldListASpecialtyNoVeterinarianHolds constructs the entity directly (`Specialty unheldSpecialty = new Specialty(); unheldSpecialty.setName(...)`) instead of going through a factory method, breaking the Three-Tier/Factory-Methods rule in docs/testing-principles.md ("Test Data Construction > Factory Methods", applies to tests written from 2026-07-31 onward). The sibling unit-test file (SpecialtyDirectoryTests) already has the pattern to copy: createASpecialty(name). A sweep of both new test files found this as the only direct-construction instance.
findings.fix: Add a private createASpecialty(String name) factory method to SpecialtyControllerTests (or a small shared test helper) and replace the direct `new Specialty()` + setter calls with it, mirroring SpecialtyDirectoryTests.createASpecialty.

findings.description: NO_HOLDERS_CELL asserts on a literal HTML fragment (`none`) taken from the rendered response body. This couples the test to the template's exact markup shape (tag choice, absence of attributes, whitespace) rather than to the acceptance behavior ("a specialty no vet holds is shown as held by no one"). A template change that keeps the same visible text but alters markup (e.g. adds a css class, or Thymeleaf renders self-closing) breaks this test without any behavior regression -- an implementation-coupled rather than behavior-coupled assertion, contrary to testing-principles.md "Fluent Assertions > Use the most direct assertion available".
findings.fix: Assert on the localized message text appearing in the row for the unheld specialty (e.g. via the message key's resolved value, or an HTML-aware query such as Jsoup/xpath scoped to the row) instead of matching a raw HTML string.

approved_aspects: SpecialtyDirectoryTests correctly isolates the read-model as a pure unit (no I/O), matching the pyramid's unit layer, and every PRD-listed test_name for the read model is present and passing.

Mocking policy fully honored: no Mockito anywhere in the new tests; SpecialtyControllerTests uses @SpringBootTest + real MockMvc + real seeded H2 data + real templates, which is stronger than the existing @MockitoBean-based VetControllerTests pattern it sits beside.

All PRD edge cases are covered by dedicated tests with correct expectations verified against the actual seed data (src/main/resources/db/h2/data.sql): James Carter and Sharon Jenkins genuinely hold no specialty, so theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOmitAVeterinarianHoldingNoSpecialty is not invented data.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldOrderItsEntriesStably and the repository-ordering test in ClinicServiceTests correctly split the ordering guarantee across layers: the unit test proves the in-memory sort, the integration test proves the @Query ORDER BY -- not redundant.

theSpecialtyDirectoryShouldCarryNoNavigationEntryOfItsOwn is a valid proxy for the PRD's "no other page links to it" criterion, because fragments/layout.html renders the identical, non-page-conditional nav list on every page that includes it -- verified by reading the fragment and vetList.html.
jacocoTestReport shows 100% line coverage (0 missed) on SpecialtyDirectory, SpecialtyDirectory.Entry, and SpecialtyController, comfortably clearing the brief's 80% domain-package target.
Whole-object AssertJ comparisons (containsExactly(new SpecialtyDirectory.Entry(...))) are used throughout SpecialtyDirectoryTests rather than field-by-field assertions, per testing-principles.md.
./gradlew test passed with all new and existing tests green.

author: doc-reviewer

findings.description: The Specialty directory paragraph states the literal route '/specialties.html' in PRD prose: "It is reachable only at its own address, /specialties.html: no navigation entry and no link from any other page is part of this capability." This is mechanism, not behavior — the litmus test in the prd-authoring skill ("would it change when switching to another language?") is met: an HTTP route mapping is exactly the kind of fact that changes with the web framework. The bounded, testable claim is already carried behaviorally by the 'Done when' bullet ('given any other page of the system, when it is rendered, then it carries no link to the specialty directory') and by the Open Question on a visible entry point — neither needs the literal string. Nowhere in system-design.md is the concrete route documented either (the Contracts row for SpecialtyController says only 'from its own route'), so the literal address currently lives only in the PRD, the one document forbidden from carrying mechanism. Rewrite the sentence to state the behavior only (reachable solely by direct navigation, no advertised entry point) and drop the literal path; the path itself needs no restatement in system-design.md, since PRD boundary violations are never autofix-eligible on docs/prd.md (document-writing skill's review-checks.md, Autofix on the PRD Path, condition 3), this routes to product-requirements-expert rather than being applied as an autofix.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Staff can see which veterinarians hold each specialty
summary: A read-only specialty directory page lists every specialty the clinic knows by its stored name, each with the veterinarians holding it, on one page that advertises no entry point.

Each veterinarian holding a specialty is shown under it by first name then last name (for example "Helen Leary").
A veterinarian holding no specialty appears nowhere on the page.
Every specialty renders together on one page; nothing offers a further page.
No other page of the system carries a link to the specialty directory.
Edge case 1: a specialty no veterinarian holds is still listed, shown as held by no one.

author: security-reviewer
approved_aspects: Fix delta verified against the actual diff (scripts/changeset.sh --base-tree 78e75f0): only docs/prd.md and src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/vet/SpecialtyControllerTests.java changed. src/main/ and build.gradle are untouched in this delta, so no production, template, dependency, or configuration surface moved since the prior approval.

No supply-chain change: build.gradle and the Gradle wrapper are absent from the delta, so the dependency set reviewed and approved on the prior pass still stands; no re-run of dependencyCheckAnalyze warranted.

The markup-stripping helper readerTextOf (SpecialtyControllerTests.java:76) cannot mask an XSS regression. It is applied only to positive AssertJ contains() assertions whose expected values are ASCII literals with no markup (UNHELD_SPECIALTY_NAME 'oncology' and the MessageSource-resolved 'none' wording), so no injected tag can be stripped into a passing match. Stripping only loosens a positive containment assertion; it cannot convert a failing escaping check into a pass, and no assertion in the file depends on escaping semantics.

Resolving the expected wording through the application MessageSource under an explicit Locale.ENGLISH, with the request locale pinned to the same value, removes a literal-HTML coupling without weakening the assertion: the build-pass record documents a mutation check (deleting the th:if none span) that fails the test.

Output escaping in the rendered surface is unchanged and safe: src/main/resources/templates/vets/specialtyList.html uses th:text for every model-derived value (entry.name, holder) and message key; a sweep of src/main/resources/templates/ found no th:utext anywhere, so all user-derived content stays HTML-escaped by Thymeleaf.
No secrets introduced: the delta adds no credential-shaped literal; the only new constants are a locale and a test specialty name.

PRD change is prose only, restating REQ-VET-003 reachability and adding design/ADR cross-links; it introduces no requirement with security consequence and does not claim any security control the code lacks.

author: change-grader
summary: add the read-only specialty directory page

blast_radius.note: Purely additive: every one of the 11 files is added-only (0 deleted lines anywhere), the three new prod classes live in the one vet package, no existing production class, mapping, template, config, or dependency is touched, and the only edit to existing code is one appended test in ClinicServiceTests. The new GET /specialties.html route is unauthenticated like every other route in this app but exposes only specialty names and vet full names already published on /vets.html.

semantic_surprise.note: Read all 17 hunks: SpecialtyDirectory.of inverts the Vet-owned association in memory by grouping vets under specialty id, sorts specialties by name then id and holders by last-then-first-then-id, formats First then Last, and copies both lists in the compact constructors, so no entity or live collection reaches the model and the cached vets list is never mutated. The controller is a two-line delegator, the repository is a parameterless ORDER BY query copying PetTypeRepository, and the template mirrors vetList.html's holder idiom with the layout menu argument specialties, which matches none of the fragment's menuItem values (home, owners, vets, error), so no nav entry lights up. Only latent oddity, unreachable in production: the comparators' getId tiebreaks would NPE on an unpersisted Specialty or Vet with a null id and a duplicate name, and null ids would collide as one map key - every instance here comes from a repository, so ids are always set.

test_adequacy.note: 273 test lines against 211 prod lines, and the tests assert real outcomes rather than restating the implementation: SpecialtyDirectoryTests exercises all three PRD edge cases with real Specialty and Vet objects and whole-record containsExactly comparisons including the defensive-copy case, SpecialtyControllerTests renders through real templates against seeded H2 (the omitted vets James Carter and Sharon Jenkins genuinely hold no specialty in data.sql), and the ClinicServiceTests addition pins the repository ORDER BY separately from the in-memory sort. The unheld-specialty assertion was mutation-checked (deleting the none span fails it) after the fix round replaced its raw-markup literal with MessageSource-resolved wording. The one soft spot is the no-inbound-link test, which only inspects the specialty page's own output, but a grep across src/main templates confirms no page anywhere links to the route.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four reviewers of the full high-risk battery approved on the second pass with zero findings and no escalate tag; the first pass's one critical bar_clause finding (a literal route in PRD prose) was fixed and re-approved by the same doc-reviewer with explicit reasoning, and the two fixable test findings were closed and re-verified by the test-reviewer. The product-requirements-expert's deliberate refusal to restate the route in system-design.md is a reasoned call the doc-reviewer independently endorsed, not a reservation left hanging.

scope_deviation.note: The changed file set matches the design-block's primary_paths exactly, plus the docs it names and one test appended in the established ClinicServiceTests location; nothing outside the vet package moved. Zero consultations and zero build retries, and the single design revision was a record-only correction adding docs/adr/README.md to supporting_paths after the autofix audit flagged it - no design decision and no code changed. The three unanswered product questions were recorded as PRD open questions under the narrowest reading rather than being resolved unilaterally.
